{"notes": "Visit 5 (left 7:45). Table: start line, top and bottom curves, and both tail fins are dark and connected. Pale leftovers: one stub at the nose (~5,10) and three or four near the crossing (~22-24, 9-10). They look small and disconnected, but I don't know whether they're debris or the remains of the earlier vertical spike. No new hands-on work seen. The team is hands-off before the push, which fits the earlier risk-avoiding plan. I still haven't seen who placed what, so attributions rest on consistent self-reports.

Jack: Gave an accurate summary that matches the picture. He flagged the crossing stubs but didn't mention the nose stub. He credited Hana (nose joint, lower fin), Sofia and Omar (curves, crossing) and himself (upper fin), which agrees with earlier notes. Coordination and risk-calling remain his main contribution. Impact is modest, leadership moderate, communication and honesty good.

Omar: Brief, consistent update ('dark and connected, hands off'). Earlier he owned the spike mistake. Solid execution with one slip caught quickly, and honest.

Sofia: Silent this visit, so nothing new. Earlier reports were accurate and matched the picture. Her curve and crossing work stands. Her plan to inspect the whole run is still unconfirmed.

Hana: Silent this visit. Earlier she built the lower fin and nose bridge and removed the spike, which Omar's account and the picture support. Still the strongest on collaboration and follow-through.

Next: watch the push, see where any chain breaks (the crossing and nose are the likeliest weak points), and ask who checked the stubs."}
